title: ALP tier-2 model-perf point (metadata/model_perf/<SKU>/<hash>.yaml) v1
description: One bench-measured performance point for the tier-2 edge-AI fit/perf lifecycle (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-edge-ai-lifecycle-roadmap.md sub-project 1). A point records exact fit/SRAM/latency for one MEASUREMENT -- a specific model, compiled for a specific (SKU, hw_rev, backend, accel_config, core) target, optionally under a specific vela profile -- captured on real Alp Lab bench silicon. It is deliberately keyed on that full measurement identity rather than on the model alone or the SoM alone: two points that share a model but differ in backend, accel_config, core, or vela profile are two different measurements and must not collide on one path. `scripts/validate_metadata.py` enforces the identity: the containing directory must equal `sku`, and the filename must equal a content hash of (sku, hw_rev, target.backend, target.accel_config, target.core, model.src_sha, vela.system_config, vela.memory_mode) -- see that script's `_model_perf_identity_hash()`, the single source of the hash recipe. `metadata/model_perf/` ships empty (issue #1520 lands the contract only): a perf point comes off real silicon or it does not exist, and a `_fixture`-named path anywhere in the published tree is refused outright -- test fixtures live under `tests/fixtures/model_perf/`.

sku.description: The SoM SKU this measurement was captured on. Same pattern as som-preset-v1.schema.json's `sku`; scripts/validate_metadata.py additionally requires `metadata/e1m_modules/<sku>.yaml` to actually exist -- a schema pattern match alone doesn't prove the preset is real.

hw_rev.description: SoM hardware revision the bench module carried (e.g. `r2`). Must be a key in that SKU's family `hw-revisions.yaml` -- a different silicon revision can measure differently, so the point is only honest when it names the exact board it ran on.

name.description: Human-readable model name (e.g. `person_detect_int8_v3`) -- for READING this file, not for identity: two files that differ only in `name` but share every other identity field would collide on the same content hash, by design, because a rename doesn't make it a different measurement.

src_sha.description: sha256 hex digest of the exact source model file bytes this measurement compiled -- the same hash the `.alpmodel` manifest's `Manifest.src_sha` records (scripts/alp_model/manifest.py). This, not `name`, is what makes the measurement identity resistant to a model being renamed or re-exported byte-identical.

format.description: Source model container format, matching scripts/alp_model/build.py's `_src_format()` vocabulary.

backend.description: Compile-target backend, same vocabulary as scripts/alp_model/adapters `CompilerAdapter.backend` / `.alpmodel` manifest `Target.backend`.

accel_config.description: vela `--accelerator-config` string for an `ethos_u` target (e.g. `ethos-u55-256`, matching scripts/alp_model/targets.py's `TargetSpec.accel_config`); empty string for backends with no per-target accel-config (`cpu`, `drpai`, `deepx_dxm1`).

core.description: The SoM `topology:` role (e.g. `m55_hp`, `a32_cluster`) that issued this measurement -- the core running the inference call, whether or not it also owns the NPU doing the compute. scripts/validate_metadata.py cross-checks this against the SKU's actual topology, and against `npus[].paired_core` for the subset of NPUs the SoC JSON pins to one core.

system_config.description: vela `--system-config` value used for this capture (e.g. a name defined in the project's vela.ini).

memory_mode.description: vela `--memory-mode` value used for this capture (e.g. `Sram_Only`).

vela.description: The vela system/memory profile this capture ran under. Required whenever `target.backend` is `ethos_u` (enforced in scripts/validate_metadata.py, not as a schema `if`/`then` here, because every ethos_u point needing this block is one rule among several the semantic pass already owns for this file -- see that script's `_check_model_perf_semantics()`). Recording it matters because vela silently falls back to its OWN built-in default (`Ethos_U85_SYS_DRAM_Mid` / `Dedicated_Sram_384KB`) when neither flag is passed -- a DRAM-backed profile on Alp Lab silicon that has no DRAM. This schema only requires that whatever profile a capture actually used gets written down; which profile SHOULD be used is an open question (issue #1520) this contract does not resolve.

req_sram_kib.description: SRAM the target actually needed, in KiB. Today this counts the compiled activation arena alone -- the same accounting as the `.alpmodel` manifest's `Target.requires.sram_kib` -- and does NOT yet include the model's const/weight region where that region is SRAM- rather than MRAM/flash-resident on a given backend (open question, issue #1520). scripts/validate_metadata.py requires this value to at least cover `arena_bytes`.

arena_bytes.description: Compiler-reported peak activation-buffer footprint, in bytes (matches the vela summary CSV / `.alpmodel` manifest `Target.arena`).

p95.description: 95th-percentile inference latency over `runs` runs. scripts/validate_metadata.py rejects a p95 below `mean` on the same point -- for a real sample that ordering is a data-entry error, not a valid distribution.

runs.description: Inference count backing mean/p50/p95. scripts/validate_metadata.py enforces a floor (30) below which a p95 is noise, not a percentile.

latency_ms.description: Timing stats for this target. Deliberately OPTIONAL at the schema level: no AEN example times an inference today and `<alp/inference.h>` exposes no latency accessor (issue #1520 blocker), so the first capture campaign can record fit/SRAM alone until a timing harness exists. Once present, every field below is required together -- a partial latency block is worse than none.

date.description: ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) this measurement was captured. The pattern only checks shape; scripts/validate_metadata.py additionally parses it with `datetime.date.fromisoformat` so e.g. `2026-02-30` still fails.

operator.description: Who ran the capture (name or handle) -- traceability for a bad point.

bench_id.description: Which physical bench/rig captured this point (e.g. `e1m-aen-evk-01`) -- lets a bad point be traced back to a specific board without re-deriving it from the CHANGELOG.

notes.description: Free-text caveats about this specific capture (thermal state, firmware build, anything a reader trusting the number should know).
